entry.title: In Sudan, the army regains ground in Kordofan, where drone strikes are killing civilians
entry.content:
Sudan’s army and its Darfuri allies have retaken several towns in West Kordofan and loosened the grip on El Obeid. Civilians are paying the price of the offensive, caught between drones and paramilitary attacks.

Sudan’s army and allied Darfuri forces have in recent days retaken several strategic towns in West Kordofan, including Al-Khuwei, breaking the siege that the Rapid Support Forces had imposed on El Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan, according to Al Jazeera. General Hemedti’s paramilitaries still hold En Nahud, a gold-mining town where they have killed ten civilians since Thursday, according to a local relief group quoted by Anadolu, while drone strikes have killed at least 15 civilians in the region in recent days, according to the Sudanese outlet Darfur24. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera expect the paramilitaries to fall back towards Darfur, their tribal heartland, as the UN describes Kordofan as the epicentre of the conflict and most humanitarian operations there have been suspended.

entry.title: In Sudan, a drone war is strangling civilians
entry.content:
More than three years into the conflict, the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces are stepping up strikes on infrastructure. The crisis is now spilling over into neighbouring Ethiopia.

The Rapid Support Forces (RSF), at war with the regular army since April 2023, seized the Sali military base in Blue Nile state on 3 November and are using drones against power stations and depots, leaving hundreds of aid lorries stranded for lack of fuel. A year after the fall of El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, Amnesty International is still documenting executions, detentions and torture there, and describes a city emptied of the vast majority of its inhabitants. The Sudanese authorities accuse Ethiopia of hosting RSF drone launch sites; Addis Ababa hit back on 4 November by expelling six Sudanese diplomats, raising fears that the conflict could spread across the Horn of Africa.
